new.n: Eccentric Scotchman Smith's buried gold, old Whitford cabin site, Fergus Falls (1862 legend)
new.pl: Old Whitford cabin cellar 'near Whitford street, inside the fence of Henry G. Page's block', Fergus Falls (1916 county history)
new.v: Gold (no amount); one gold sovereign later found
new.st: The county history tells of an eccentric Scotchman named Smith who lived at the Whitford cabin on the Fergus Falls townsite and was killed by Indians in 1862; a tale grew that he buried gold on the townsite, and a gold sovereign was later found near the old cabin. By 1916 the cabin cellar lay 'near Whitford street, inside the fence of Henry G. Page's block'. Pin is the block area, not the spot itself.
new.t: One county-history telling; a single sovereign found. Urban lot in Fergus Falls: look only.
src: Mason, History of Otter Tail County, Minnesota (1916), vol. 1, pp. 684-686
pinev: Placed on the 1916 description of the Page block near Whitford St; no Whitford St in today's MnGeo address points, so the block is fixed from the county history only (r300). A Sanborn check of the Page block is queued.

new.n: 'Bogus Camp' counterfeiters' hideout, bluffs of sec 33, Town of Franklin (1850s)
new.pl: Rock pocket under the bluffs, sec 33 T10N R4E, Town of Franklin, Sauk Co (1880 county history)
new.v: Counterfeiting relics (dies, bogus coin, forge scrap)
new.st: The 1880 county history places a counterfeiters' 'Bogus Camp' in a rock pocket under the bluffs in sec 33 T10N R4E, Town of Franklin, with a spring, a cabin, a forge and a die-press set in a tree. Pin is the section, not the spot itself.
new.t: Relic site (dies, bogus coin, forge scrap), not a cache; county history only. Private bluff land: permission.
src: History of Sauk County, Wisconsin (Western Historical Co., 1880), p. 409
pinev: Sec 33 T10N R4E from the 1880 county history; pin in the section, r800.

new.st: The county history says Ossian was a rendezvous for a gang of counterfeiters in the 1850s who passed bogus gold pieces. Pin is the town only.
new.t: Record only; no cache named. Town lots.
src: History of Winneshiek and Allamakee Counties, Iowa (1882) / Alexander (1877), pp. 130-132
pinev: Iowa Populated Places point for Ossian (43.1464,-91.7646); town only, r1500.

new.n: Counterfeiters' den at Lyons, dies thrown into the Grand River (1835-36)
new.pl: Lyons, Ionia Co, on the Grand River (town only)
new.v: Counterfeiting dies thrown in the river
new.st: In 1835-36 a counterfeiters' den operated at Lyons; when broken up, the dies were thrown into the Grand River. Pin is the town only.
new.t: Relic target in the river bed, not a cache; county history only. River: look only.
src: History of Ionia and Montcalm Counties, Michigan (1881), p. 240
pinev: Centre of the Census place outline for Lyons village (GNIS not reachable from here); town only, r500.

new.n: 'Sodom and Gomorrah' saloons, counterfeiters' nest near Hardin, Monona Twp (1850s)
new.pl: Near Hardin, Monona Twp, Clayton Co (place point)
new.st: The 1916 county history recalls two saloons near Hardin, Monona Twp, nicknamed Sodom and Gomorrah, as a nest of counterfeiters in early days. Pin is the place only.
new.t: Record only; no cache named. Private land.
src: Price, History of Clayton County, Iowa (1916)
pinev: Iowa Populated Places point for Hardin, Clayton Co (43.0803,-91.4843); place only, r1500.
